children: said Tuesday it redeemed $250 million of senior notes, renewed a major financing facility and began buying back shares as the lawn and garden products company works to reduce debt while returning capital to stockholders.

The company redeemed all of its 5.25% senior notes due in 2026 on Sept. 11. It funded the repayment with borrowings under its revolving credit facility and excess free cash flow expected during fiscal 2026.

also renewed a $750 million accounts receivable facility with J.P. Morgan Chase, extending its maturity through Aug. 31, 2027. Such facilities let companies obtain liquidity using customer receivables and can help support working-capital needs.
For investors, the debt repayment removes a near-term maturity but does not eliminate the obligation because ScottsMiracle-Gro

partly replaced the notes with revolver borrowings. The company’s projected $275 million in free cash flow could help reduce that balance. Meanwhile, the buyback may support per-share results, though management said debt reduction will take priority over additional repurchases.

spent $25 million repurchasing shares in August, beginning a previously authorized $500 million program. The company said the pace and size of future purchases will depend on market conditions, leverage goals and other financial priorities.

The company reaffirmed its fiscal 2026 forecast, including low-single-digit sales growth in its U.S. Consumer business, adjusted gross margin of at least 32% and adjusted earnings of $4.30 to $4.45 a share. It continues to expect mid-single-digit adjusted EBITDA growth, $275 million in free cash flow and a year-end leverage ratio in the high-three-times range.
fiscal year ends Sept. 30. The company plans to report its full-year results on Nov. 4.
